figures.caption: Fig. 1.1: Boundary-layer localization of nonuniqueness in non-auxiliary A-B and AM discovery systems. To illustrate the algebraic kernel structure, we use the scalar time-dependent relation ẋ = f(t) on [0, 1], with randomly sampled values of f on the uniform grid. This simplification affects only the presentation of the example, since the kernel localization depends on the LMM discovery matrix. For each scheme, three representative zero-residual solutions are plotted.
Fig. 5.1: Mean trajectory error etraj over random seeds for A-B schemes. Dashed lines are scaled reference slopes with rates p = 1, 2, 3.
Fig. 5.2: Mean trajectory error etraj over random seeds for A-M schemes. Dashed lines are scaled reference slopes with rates p = 2, 3, 4.
